SERVICES

Architecture first. Capacity second.

Most QA spend goes into more tests on an unstable base. We invert that: a centralized framework, then pods that ship against it.

Playwright

Playwright test architecture

One system of record for fixtures, auth, traces, and reporting — not a suite per squad.

Layered page objects and test IDs that survive product redesigns
Shared auth, seed, and environment contracts instead of copy-paste helpers
Parallelization mapped to CI budget, with traces you can actually debug
A documented ownership model so the framework does not fork in Q3

CI / CD

CI/CD pipeline integration

PR gates that encode risk, not theater. Green means shippable.

Sharding, artifact retention, and retry policy with a stated cause
Selectors for smoke vs. deep suites so merge queues stay honest
Failure taxonomy wired into Slack/Jira without becoming noise
Earlier signal in the loop — the mechanism behind 3× delivery velocity

Reliability

Test flakiness eradication

Flake is an SLO. We put a budget, an owner, and a quarantine path on it.

Root-cause classes: race, environment, selector, data, third-party
Deterministic waits and network stubs where the product is not the test
Quarantine with expiry — no eternal skipped specs
Dashboards that make <2% flake a managed number, not a wish

SDET pods

Distributed SDET pods

Embedded engineers, your backlog, our platform. Capacity without a hiring freeze.

Pods staffed against the shared architecture, not a private toolbox
Coverage mapped to risk: money paths, auth, migrations, release trains
Knowledge transfer written into the engagement, not left as folklore
A quality function that behaves like platform engineering

Platform

Framework ownership

We keep the platform current after the standing-up is done.

Playwright and browser-matrix upgrades on a cadence
Pipeline health, flake tax, and office hours with your squads
Guardrails so new tests land in the architecture, not beside it
The monthly retainer is ownership, not a ticket dump

HOW IT WORKS

How a director should buy quality work.

Short discovery. Written architecture. Then either a standing platform, embedded pods, or both. No retainers that exist to 'stay in the mix.'

01

Audit the real constraint

We read the pipeline, the flake report, and the merge queue — not a slide about 'quality culture.' You get a written diagnosis of architecture debt vs. staffing debt.

02

Stand up the platform

Fixtures, auth, reporting, and CI contracts land as a shared system. Squads stop inventing private helpers. This is the setup retainer.

03

Staff pods against it

Distributed SDET capacity runs on the platform we just made non-optional. Ownership stays with Testing Explained or transfers with a runbook — your call.

PRICING

Setup retainers and monthly ownership. Stated as numbers.

Directors should be able to take this to finance without a 'let's hop on a call to discuss packages' fog. Scope is still scoped — the bands are real.

Framework Setup

upfront, typically 3–5 weeks

A one-time architecture engagement. We replace scattered suites with a Playwright system of record and wire it into CI.

Current-state audit of tests, pipelines, and flake sources

Handoff runbook for your staff engineers

Platform Ownership

ONGOING

Most orgs keep this

$2.5K–$3.5K/mo

per month, after setup

Ongoing ownership of the platform. We keep Playwright current, hold the flake SLO, and keep new tests inside the architecture.

Flake SLO ownership and quarantine with expiry
Playwright and browser-matrix upgrades
Pipeline health and merge-queue hygiene
Office hours with squads shipping against the platform
Monthly written status — numbers, not narrative

Month-to-month after the first 30 days. This is maintenance of a system, not a body shop.

Combined engagements (setup plus the first quarter of ownership) are the usual starting point. SDET pods are scoped separately against the same platform — we will not staff a pod onto a framework we would not operate.

FAQ

Questions directors ask before the call.
Why not just hire in-house?
+

Setup ends with a handoff runbook so your staff engineers own the platform. Pods are additional capacity against that same system, scoped separately, when you need it.

Does this work if we use Cypress?
+

The platform we stand up is Playwright. If Cypress is what you run today, that is where the audit starts.

How fast do we see results?
+

Framework Setup is a one-time engagement, typically 3–5 weeks, at $5K–$10K. The site does not promise a result date beyond that window.

What happens after setup?
+

Platform Ownership is $2.5K–$3.5K per month after setup, month-to-month after the first 30 days. SDET pods are scoped separately against the same platform.

How are SDET pods priced?
+

Priced after the audit.
